The simulation is a 2D lid-driven cavity flow of an incompressible fluid using OpenFOAM with the icoFoam solver.
The cavity is 0.1 m wide in x and 0.1 m high in y, extruded 0.01 m in z with a single cell thickness, and the front and back z-faces use empty boundary conditions to enforce two-dimensionality.
The mesh is generated with blockMesh using vertices at (0 0 0), (0.1 0 0), (0.1 0.1 0), and (0 0.1 0), with a single hex block of cell counts (20 20 1) and uniform grading (no wall refinement).
The mesh has three patches: movingWall (top boundary), fixedWalls (bottom, left, and right boundaries combined), and frontAndBack (front and back z-faces).
The fluid is incompressible with kinematic viscosity nu = 0.001 m²/s specified in constant/transportProperties.
The movingWall patch has velocity fixedValue uniform (1 0 0) in 0/U and zeroGradient pressure in 0/p.
The fixedWalls patch uses the noSlip type for velocity in 0/U and zeroGradient for pressure in 0/p.
The frontAndBack patch uses empty boundary conditions for both U and p.
Initial conditions are uniform (0 0 0) for velocity and uniform 0 for pressure throughout the domain.
The system/controlDict specifies application icoFoam, startFrom startTime, startTime 0, endTime 0.5, deltaT 0.002, writeControl timeStep, and writeInterval 20.
This gives a total of 250 time steps with results written every 20 steps (every 0.04 s of simulated time), producing 25 written time directories.
The target Reynolds number is Re = U·L/nu = (1 m/s × 0.1 m) / 0.001 m²/s = 100, a laminar regime consistent with icoFoam.
The system/fvSchemes and system/fvSolution files use the standard icoFoam tutorial defaults (second-order schemes and standard PISO settings).
